note: Track note-names, step 4: naming notes fast, first on the neck game with no clock, then from the staff-reading game one note per click, then the neck game with its sharps and flats on a faster click. The staff-reading game takes the place of a plain staff, which never asks for a note's name, and the old Key selector of the last section is gone: the tempo is moves, the faster section keeping its distance. Missing: staff-reading asks natural notes only, so the sharps and flats are named on the neck.

exercise.title: Note names without stopping to think
exercise.why: A metronome gives each name one beat to arrive, so you stop counting up from a note you know and start seeing each note as its own name.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below: it lights one spot on the guitar neck, and you pick its note name from the buttons under it.
Answer as fast as you can read the spot.
Practice until most names come before you count frets.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Then press Start in the game under it: it draws one note on the staff, and you press its letter.
Press one letter on each click, every note in time.
If a name comes late, let that click go and answer on the next one.

Press Play below to start the metronome, a little faster now. Then press Start in the game under it: the lit spots on the neck are sharps and flats too.
Pick one name on each click, and pick the whole name: the sharp or the flat is part of it.
Practice until the sharps and flats come as quickly as the plain letters.
